- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

input.prompt:
In this repository, find every server-side location that enforces "memo visibility" — i.e., logic that decides whether a given user/actor is allowed to VIEW a memo (as opposed to create/edit/delete). This includes things like:
- API route handlers / controllers that fetch a memo by id and check permissions before returning it
- Database query filters (e.g. WHERE clauses) that restrict which memos are returned based on visibility/audience
- Middleware or authorization helper functions specifically checking memo visibility
- GraphQL resolvers for memos
- WebSocket/realtime subscription handlers for memos
- Any background job, search/index endpoint, or export endpoint that also needs to filter memos by visibility

Search broadly for the term "memo" across the codebase (routes, services, models, resolvers, sql). For each distinct visibility check found, report:
1. The enforcement mechanism (short description)
2. The exact file path
3. The relevant function/symbol name and approximate line number
4. A short code snippet or description of the check logic (e.g. "checks memo.visibility === 'private' && memo.authorId !== userId")

Be thorough - check for at least 3-5 distinct sites since memo visibility could be enforced in multiple places (e.g., the main GET endpoint, a search/list endpoint, a GraphQL resolver, a real-time subscription, an export feature). List all files that contain visibility-related logic for memos, even if some turn out to be duplicates of the same check pattern.

content.text:
h15.

Memo view/read visibility is re-implemented independently (not via one shared guard) in each of these server surfaces:

enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39 (`checkMemoReadAccess`, used by `GetMemo` at line 356/367 and by `memo_service_comments.go:148`)
enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30,38,83 (`ListMemoReactions`/`UpsertMemoReaction` duplicate private/creator check before exposing reactions)
enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:445,451 (linked-attachment access follows memo visibility, separate copy of the check)
enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214,222 (another duplicate copy for `ListMemoAttachments`)
enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41 (comment creation checks `relatedMemo.Visibility` before allowing/exposing comment)
enforcement site — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650-704 (`checkAttachmentPermission`, a separate HTTP file-serving surface with its own visibility check plus share-token/anonymous-access bypass logic)
enforcement site — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134 (`canReceive`, filters realtime SSE broadcast events to clients based on `event.Visibility`/creator)
enforcement site — store/db/postgres/memo.go:89, store/db/mysql/memo.go, store/db/sqlite/memo.go (DB-level `WHERE` filtering via `FindMemo.VisibilityList`, the query-layer backstop used by `ListMemos`/RSS/frontend SSR)

Supporting/derived call sites that build the `VisibilityList`/filter string consumed by the DB layer above (not independent checks, but distinct call sites deciding what's queryable):
- server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:219-225 (`ListMemos`)
- server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90,218-220
- server/router/rss/rss.go:90,141 (public-only RSS feed)
- server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150 (public-only SSR meta tags)
- server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:184-186, memo_relation_service.go:109-111, memo_service_comments.go:158-160

Related (content-exposure rather than view-gate, worth noting): `server/notification/email.go:313-316` and `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312` also re-check `memo.Visibility` to decide whether to include memo content in emails/in-app notifications, and `memo_mention_helpers.go:62-84` re-checks it before notifying a mentioned user.
